column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the animal “a calf, a son of the herd”; BSB says “a young bull.”
The Hebrew calls the calf and lamb “sons of a year”; BSB gives their age as “a year old.”
The Hebrew uses the plural “peace offerings”; BSB says “a peace offering.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew gives repeated commands to make atonement, alongside the commands to offer the sacrifices; BSB expresses the atonement clauses as purposes with “to make atonement.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he poured out “the blood”; BSB specifies “the rest of the blood.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says he burned the flesh and hide “with fire”; BSB omits that phrase.
The Hebrew has an unnamed “he” and explicitly calls the sons “the sons of Aaron”; BSB names Aaron as the slaughterer and then says “His sons.”
The Hebrew joins the pieces and “the head” with “and”; BSB says “including the head.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins with an unnamed “he”; BSB supplies “Aaron.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he “filled his palm” from the offering; BSB says he “took a handful.”
The Hebrew repeats “the sons of Aaron”; BSB says “His sons.”
The Hebrew says “the covering,” without explicitly naming the entrails here; BSB specifies “the fat covering the entrails.”
The Hebrew says “he” burned the fat portions; BSB supplies “Aaron.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Aaron as the one waving the portions; BSB continues with “he.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they fell “on their faces”; BSB condenses the bodily expression to “facedown.”
